title: Supercapacitor pseudocapacitance gives planar cells pillar-level charge
idea: Borrowed from supercapacitors: replace the 70:1 MIM pillar with a shallow cup lined by a 5-nm hydrous RuO2 or Ti3C2 MXene electrode against a 2-nm proton-conducting solid electrolyte (e.g., hydrated Zr-phosphate). Faradaic surface-redox capacitance of ~50-100 uF/cm2 versus ~3-5 uF/cm2 for ZrO2 MIM means a 30-nm cup only ~60 nm deep (AR~2) stores ~5 fF.
why: Fact 1 capacitor charge wall: ~20-30x higher areal capacitance cuts pillar aspect ratio from ~70:1 to ~2-5:1, deleting the hardest etch/support steps; open questions are whether proton redox completes in <10 ns and whether self-discharge stays sub-fA.

title: CMOS image-sensor pinned photodiode as a near-zero-dark-current storage well
idea: Copy the 4T image-sensor pixel: hold the bit as electrons in a fully depleted buried n-well capped by a p+ pinning layer, moved in and out through a transfer gate with complete charge transfer, so the stored charge never touches the Si/SiO2 interface where SRH generation lives. Image sensors routinely reach <1 e-/s dark current per pixel (~1e-19 A) versus the ~13 fA DRAM leakage tail.
why: Fact 3 refresh: leakage 3-5 orders lower stretches retention from 64 ms to minutes, removing most of the ~46 fJ/bit refresh and 10-20% bandwidth loss; trade is a smaller full-well (~2-5k e- at 100 nm) that needs a more sensitive sense amp.

title: Airport baggage conveyor: vertical charge-coupled bit strings in 3D stacks
idea: Like bags riding a conveyor to one scanner, deposit a 3D-NAND-style stack of 64-128 gate layers around a vertical wide-gap channel (e.g., Ga2O3 or ZnSnO) and clock charge packets up and down it CCD-style; a single sense/restore node at the top of each string reads and rewrites packets as they pass. A bit is a potential well under a gate, so each tier costs one deposition, not a transistor plus capacitor.
why: Facts 2 and 4: 3D density without a 3D capacitor or lateral transistor; ~100 tiers at 3 gates/bit gives ~30 bits per hole, ~5-10x density with no added EUV; serial shift (~1 ns/stage) keeps average latency ~20-30 ns only if strings stay short.

title: Heat-assisted magnetic recording logic: heat-gated thermionic write barrier
idea: As HAMR writes high-coercivity media only while a laser heats the spot, isolate the storage node behind a ~1.0 eV conduction-band-offset barrier (Si node under an AlN or Ga2O3 spacer) that is opaque at 300 K, and write with a 2-ns pulse in an integrated TaN microheater that lifts the barrier region to ~600 K, where thermionic emission rises ~1e8x.
why: Fact 3: hold-state leakage over a 1 eV barrier is ~1e8 below the write-state current, enabling refresh-free retention; 50-nm heaters have ~1-5 ns thermal time constants, but heater energy (~10-100 fJ) must be shared row-wide to beat refresh savings.

title: Long/short hedge: split-pillar dipole bit cancels common-mode leakage
idea: Like a market-neutral long/short position, store each bit as +Q/-Q on two halves of one pillar capacitor split by a vertical dielectric fin, accessed by twin transistors in the same active area; leakage and temperature drift hit both halves almost equally, so the difference decays far slower, and the sense amp compares the halves with no reference.
why: Facts 3 and 10: differential read doubles signal per pillar and tolerates ~3-5x more common-mode leakage, stretching refresh 4-8x; half-swing operation allows ~30% lower VARY for ~2x CV2 savings, at ~20% area cost versus 6F2.

title: Goto's parametron revived: bits as oscillation phase in pumped nanoresonators
idea: The 1950s parametron stored a bit as the 0 or pi phase of a parametrically pumped resonator; build rows of ~200-nm GHz NEMS beams (or compact LC tanks) driven at 2f by one shared row pump, so parametric bistability holds the phase while pumped and reading is a nondestructive phase comparison against a reference tone.
why: Facts 1 and 3: the bit is a dynamical state, not stored charge, so there is no capacitor and no refresh; pump power (~nW per high-Q resonator) beats 46 fJ/bit refresh only for Q>1e4, so it suits hot-buffer tiers rather than bulk capacity.

title: Williams tube reborn: field-emitter array writes charge spots on continuous film
idea: Revive the 1947 Williams tube (the first DRAM) with field-emission-display Spindt tip arrays: in a vacuum-sealed package each tip is electrostatically deflected over a 4x4 patch to write and read charge spots on an unpatterned SiO2 electret film over a sense grid, reading by secondary-emission contrast. The storage plane needs no per-bit transistor, capacitor or lithography.
why: Facts 4 and 7: the storage plane is a blanket film, so patterned features per bit drop ~16x (16 bits per tip); charge on high-quality oxide in vacuum leaks negligibly; vacuum packaging and tip lifetime are the risks.

title: Glow-in-the-dark phosphor traps: optically erased deep-trap charge bit
idea: Persistent phosphors (SrAl2O4:Eu,Dy) hold electrons in Dy-type traps for hours; dope a thin wide-gap film over a readout channel with one engineered deep trap (~1.0-1.3 eV), fill it electrically through a thin barrier, and empty it with a sub-ns pulse from an integrated micro-LED/waveguide (optically stimulated detrapping, as in OSL dosimeters) instead of high-field tunneling erase.
why: Fact 3: deep-trap retention of seconds to hours removes most refresh, and avoiding Fowler-Nordheim erase stress is the bet for flash-beating endurance (>=1e12); optical routing area and write speed are open questions.

title: LCD chemistry: ferroelectric nematic liquid as a self-healing high-k dielectric
idea: Borrow display liquid crystals: fill a shallow cup capacitor with a ferroelectric nematic LC (RM734/DIO class, Ps ~6 uC/cm2, low-frequency permittivity ~1e3-1e4) confined in a 5-nm gap between alignment layers; as a liquid it cannot fatigue or crack, and breakdown spots self-heal by flow.
why: Fact 1 needs k~70; even if GHz-range permittivity is 10-100x below the static value, k>=100 cuts AR below 10:1; speculative because polarization response at ~10 ns in nanoconfinement and ionic leakage are unproven.

title: Mercury thermometer and electrowetting display: liquid-metal nanomeniscus bit
idea: Seal a gallium-alloy nanodroplet in a 20-nm SiO2 nanochannel with two pockets; electrocapillary actuation (as in electrowetting displays) pushes the meniscus into one pocket, where it bridges or opens a gap between two electrodes, and surface-tension pinning at a constriction holds it with zero power. Read is a resistance check; the liquid reforms perfectly every cycle.
why: Facts 3 and 9: nonvolatile, refresh-free and immune to row-hammer charge coupling; a liquid has no wear mechanism, so endurance could exceed 1e15; Ga oxidation and wetting control at 20 nm are the risks.

title: Pumped-hydro twin reservoirs: fixed electron shuttled between paired quantum dots
idea: Like pumped hydro moving the same water between two reservoirs, each cell holds a fixed electron that never leaves the cell, only shifting between two coupled 2-4-nm Si nanodots (~0.3 eV charging energy) across a tunnel barrier; a write gate tilts the double well and an electrometer gate senses which dot is occupied.
why: Facts 3 and 8: with no path to a bitline there is no junction leakage to refresh, and read is non-destructive (no restore after 128x overfetch); RT operation needs sub-5-nm dots with uniform barriers, the key risk.

title: Quipu knots: topological polar textures as unknottable bits
idea: Inca quipu stored data in knots that cannot untie by accident; store a bit as the topological charge of a polar skyrmion or vortex in a 20-nm oxide-superlattice nanodisk (PbTiO3/SrTiO3, or lead-free BaTiO3/SrTiO3), which cannot relax continuously to the trivial state, switched by a field pulse from a top tip electrode and read by its distinct capacitance or tunneling conductance.
why: Facts 1 and 3: density set by texture size (~10 nm) rather than capacitor charge, and topology gives non-volatility without fatigue-prone domain-wall sweeps; write fields, read contrast and RT stability at 10 nm are unproven.

title: Refrigerator crisper drawer: thermoelectrically chilled cell array only
idea: Keep only the drawer cold, not the kitchen: integrate a thin-film SiGe or Bi2Te3 thermoelectric layer under the cell-array mats only, holding storage nodes ~25-30 K below the periphery and logic, with heat pumped into the package lid. Junction leakage roughly halves every ~8-10 K.
why: Fact 3: a 25 K drop cuts leakage ~6-8x, stretching refresh from 32 ms to ~200 ms; net gain requires array idle power share >20% and thermoelectric COP >~0.5 at small dT; SiGe avoids tellurium supply risk.

title: Dam spillways: self-limiting overflow barriers quantize multi-level charge
idea: Borrow the image sensor's anti-blooming drain and a dam's spillway: each storage node gets a gate-controlled lateral overflow barrier whose height, set by the write voltage on the spill gate, caps stored charge at 1/3, 2/3 or full; writing deliberately overfills and the excess spills, so each cell lands on the exact level without a program-verify loop.
why: Cost per bit: 2 bits per cell with self-calibrated levels removes the cell-to-cell variation that kills DRAM MLC, ~1.6-2x bits per mm2 at the same lithography; needs a 3-threshold sense amp and somewhat larger node.

title: Croissant lamination and MLCCs: multilayer electrodes inside a shallow hole
idea: Copy multilayer ceramic capacitors and laminated pastry: in a shallow AR~15 hole, ALD-deposit four alternating TiN/ZrO2 layers, then tie odd electrodes to the node and even ones to the plate using a selective recess etch and self-aligned sidewall contacts at the rim, so capacitance multiplies by the number of dielectric interfaces.
why: Fact 1: three parallel dielectric layers give ~3x capacitance per footprint, allowing ~20:1 instead of 70:1 pillars and shorter lateral capacitors for 3D DRAM; contacting alternate layers is the process risk.

title: Neon-lamp bistability via broken-gap 2D Esaki diode latch
idea: Early computers latched bits in neon lamps' negative resistance; build a cell where two series broken-gap tunnel diodes (e.g., black phosphorus/SnSe2 or WSe2/SnSe2) form a Goto-pair bistable node with pA valley current, plus one access transistor, so the node self-restores like SRAM in ~3F2 with no refresh.
why: Fact 3 and SRAM density: static, refresh-free storage with standby current 100-1000x below SRAM; III-V tunneling SRAM failed on peak-to-valley ratio, so the bet is 2D broken-gap junctions with PVR>10 at room temperature.

title: Photochromic sunglasses: electrically switched diarylethene molecular bit
idea: Diarylethenes flip between open (insulating) and closed (conjugated, ~100x more conductive) isomers; anchor a monolayer in a 10-nm crossbar junction and switch it by field-assisted electrochemical ring closing/opening at ~1-2 V instead of light, reading conductance nondestructively, with thousands of molecules per bit for statistical robustness.
why: Density and capital: storage defined by a molecular monolayer at crossbar 4F2 with relaxed litho, thermally bistable and non-volatile; fatigue (~1e4-1e5 cycles today) must improve by ~1e10 to be DRAM-class.

title: Weather vane rotors: dipolar molecular rotors locked in crystalline cages
idea: Amphidynamic crystals and MOFs hold polar rotors (e.g., difluorophenylene on a rigid axle) that point like weather vanes; engineer a two-fold rotational potential with ~0.8-1.0 eV barrier, grow an oriented 10-nm MOF film as the cell dielectric, and switch rotor orientation with a field pulse so the net polarization shifts a readout capacitance or channel threshold.
why: Ferroelectric-like non-volatility without oxide fatigue, since each rotor flips independently with no vacancy-pinned domain walls, and the barrier is chemically tunable; the speed-versus-retention trade is unproven.

title: Optical Bragg mirror for electrons: superlattice blocks hold-state leakage
idea: Insert an epitaxial Si/SiGe (or AlGaN/GaN) superlattice into the storage-node leakage path designed so electrons at hold bias fall in a minigap and are Bragg-reflected, while at write bias a miniband aligns and transmits resonantly, making an electron energy filter that acts as a check valve.
why: Fact 3: suppresses band-to-band and trap-assisted tunneling (GIDL) at hold by ~100-1000x while keeping ns writes; coherent miniband transport through ~10 periods at room temperature is the physics risk.

title: SOI-wafer supply model: capacitor arrays shipped under transferred silicon
idea: Copy the engineered-substrate business behind SOI wafers: a specialist supplier fabricates the deep-trench/ high-k storage-capacitor array (with alignment marks) on depreciated 65-nm-class tools, then layer-transfers a thin crystalline Si film on top by Smart-Cut bonding; the DRAM fab aligns and builds access transistors and periphery in that film.
why: Fact 4 capital: moves the high-AR capacitor module out of the leading-edge DRAM fab, decouples capacitor thermal budget from transistors (allowing >900 C crystallization for higher k), and creates a U.S. supplier tier; overlay through the transferred film is the main risk.

title: Single-photon avalanche diode logic: Geiger-mode read of a 300-electron node
idea: Treat the storage node as a gate over a tiny Geiger-mode avalanche junction: the stored charge shifts local breakdown by ~0.3 V, and the read biases between the two breakdown voltages for ~2 ns so a self-quenched avalanche (a large digital pulse) fires only for one state, as in SPAD pixels.
why: Fact 1: digital-gain sensing needs ~0.2-0.5 fF instead of ~5 fF, collapsing capacitor height 10-20x; dark-count false fires (~1e-7 per ns window) and afterpulsing demand ECC and are the risk.

title: League-table standings: rank-modulated bits immune to uniform charge loss
idea: A league table cares who is ahead, not absolute points: group six cells and encode data in the permutation order of their charges (rank modulation), written by charging each cell just above the previous one and read by a winner-take-all comparator tree; uniform leakage shrinks all charges together without changing the order.
why: Fact 3 and density: refresh is needed only when leakage differences flip an order, ~3-10x longer intervals, and log2(6!)=9.5 bits per 6 cells gives ~1.6 bits/cell (~1.5x density) at the cost of a comparator tree in the sense amp.

title: TOPCon solar contact: tunnel-oxide passivating junction for the storage node
idea: High-efficiency solar cells reach surface recombination velocities <1 cm/s with a 1.5-nm SiO2 tunnel oxide under doped poly-Si (TOPCon); replace the storage-node contact's implanted n+/p junction with this carrier-selective passivating contact plus solar-style hydrogenation, so the node interface has ~100x fewer generation centers.
why: Fact 3: SRH generation at the node junction feeds the 13 fA tail; 10-100x lower interface generation lengthens worst-cell retention ~5-20x, using solar-industry tools that are abundant and U.S.-buildable.

title: Deck of cards: sliding-ferroelectric bilayer stacking flips store bits
idea: Shuffle cards by one atom: in parallel-stacked bilayer hBN or 3R-MoS2, AB versus BA stacking gives opposite out-of-plane polarization, switched by ~1 V across ~1 nm as one layer slides a third of a lattice spacing; build cells from exfoliated or CVD bilayers with e-beam-defined gates and read the polarization as a threshold shift in a stacked MoS2 channel.
why: Endurance and voltage floor (Fact 10): sliding ferroelectricity shows little wake-up/fatigue because no ions or vacancies move, giving non-volatility at ~1 V with potentially >1e12 cycles; a transfer stage, e-beam and evaporator are the whole toolset.

title: Vacuum flask isolation: NEMS relay access switch with zero off-current
idea: A thermos blocks heat by removing the medium; block leakage the same way: connect the storage capacitor to the bitline through a ~200-nm TiN or poly-SiC cantilever relay in a sealed nanocavity, closed electrostatically by the wordline and open (vacuum gap) at rest, built with e-beam litho, sputtered TiN, sacrificial SiO2 and HF-vapor release.
why: Fact 3: off-state current is truly zero, so only capacitor dielectric leakage (~aA) remains and refresh nearly vanishes, and VARY is no longer tied to transistor Vt; contact wear and stiction (~1e10 cycles shown) are the risk for DRAM endurance.

title: E-ink capsule shrunk: electrophoretic nanoparticle shuttles between nanowell electrodes
idea: Each cell is a 30-nm e-beam-defined nanowell sealed by ALD, holding one charged 5-nm Au or TiO2 nanoparticle in a low-viscosity dielectric fluid; a write pulse drives it to the top or bottom electrode (~10 ns over 15 nm at 1e8 V/m), where van der Waals adhesion holds it like E-ink pigment, and read is the capacitance change or tunneling current through the particle.
why: Non-volatile, refresh-free and immune to row-hammer charge disturb, with no material fatigue; buildable with e-beam, ALD and colloid drop-casting; nanoscale liquid sealing and particle aggregation are the risks.

title: Pulse-power antiferroelectric capacitors: ZrO2 biased at its field-induced transition
idea: Pulse-power capacitors exploit antiferroelectric ceramics whose permittivity peaks at the AFE-to-FE transition; ALD a ZrO2-rich Hf(1-x)Zr(x)O2 film (x~0.7-0.9) and shift its transition field into the cell's 0-to-VARY window with asymmetric TiN/RuO2 electrodes (work-function offset plus interface dipoles), so operation rides the steep P-E segment where k_eff reaches ~60-100.
why: Fact 1: k~70 is exactly what stops AR growth, letting AR fall from ~70 to ~35:1 at 5 fF; provable with university ALD, sputter and RTA; hysteresis loss and fatigue near the transition are the risks.

title: Mood-ring molecules: spin-crossover film switches capacitance bistably
idea: Like a mood ring, Fe(II)-triazole spin-crossover complexes switch between low-spin and high-spin states with a 10-30 K hysteresis loop near room temperature and a large dielectric and volume change; thermally evaporate or spin-coat a 10-nm film between Pt electrodes, park the die inside the loop, write with a ns field/Joule pulse, and read the capacitance shift.
why: Non-volatile inside the loop with no ion migration, and switching has been shown on ns optical timescales; needs only an evaporator, spin coater and e-beam; endurance and a narrow thermal window are the risks.

title: Setting gelatin: glass-transition-locked ions freeze a double-layer bit
idea: Like gelatin that flows warm and sets cold, spin-coat a polymerized ionic liquid (Tg ~60-80 C) as the gate dielectric of a thin channel: a ns local heater pulse lifts it above Tg, the gate voltage forms an electric double layer (~10 uF/cm2), and on cooling the ions freeze in place, holding a doping-like state with no electronic leakage path; read is the channel conductance.
why: Retention without access-transistor leakage (the charge sits in immobile ions) plus giant areal capacitance for tiny cells; made with spin coater, e-beam and evaporator; thermal crosstalk and ~10s of fJ heating per write are the risks.

title: Electrolytic capacitor trick: anodized porous niobium with self-healing oxide
idea: Electrolytic capacitors win with porous foil plus an anodic oxide that regrows over any defect; sputter Nb through a self-ordered porous-alumina template to form nanorod electrodes, grow the Nb2O5 dielectric (k~40) by room-temperature anodization (~2.5 nm/V, self-limiting), and periodically 're-form' arrays with a slight over-bias that heals leakage sites.
why: Facts 1 and 3: litho-free high-area electrodes and a self-limiting, self-healing high-k dielectric made in a beaker instead of ALD, attacking cost and the leakage tail; Nb comes from Brazil/Canada, avoiding tantalum sourcing; needs only sputter, anodization bath and furnace.

title: Solar-cell black silicon: litho-free nanograss electrodes multiply capacitor area
idea: Solar cells use maskless cryogenic SF6/O2 RIE to grow self-masked 'black silicon' needles 1-2 um tall at ~100-nm spacing; apply the same etch to texture each capacitor's bottom electrode for a 10-20x area gain, then line it conformally by ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN so each cell pad needs only coarse contact lithography.
why: Facts 1 and 4: 10-20x capacitance per footprint without EUV or a patterned high-AR etch, using one ICP-RIE plus ALD; Poisson variation in needle count sets a ~100-nm minimum pad, so it fits relaxed-pitch U.S. commodity or gain-cell storage.

title: Triboelectric generators: contact-electrified charge patches store bits
idea: Triboelectric nanogenerators move a saturating charge between dissimilar surfaces on contact; let an e-beam-defined, electrostatically actuated Ti cantilever tap a PTFE- or Al2O3-coated pad above a sensing transistor, transferring a self-limiting ~50-500 e- charge per contact, and reverse it by tapping with an opposite-polarity material, the patch retaining charge with electret-grade stability.
why: Electret retention (years) removes refresh, and the self-limiting transfer tolerates actuator variation; buildable with e-beam, sputter and sacrificial release; small charge per contact, wear and ns actuation are the risks.

title: Coin-counting purse: single-electron box stores countable electron numbers
idea: Count coins instead of weighing gold: couple a 3-5-nm Si or Pt island (e-beam litho plus oxidation thinning, or ALD nanoparticle) through one tunnel junction to a reservoir so Coulomb blockade (>150 meV charging energy) makes occupancy discrete; each cell stores 0-3 extra electrons (2 bits), read by a nearby single-electron transistor electrometer without disturbing the count.
why: Fact 10 and energy: writes of a few electrons at ~0.2 V are attojoule-scale and multi-level states are quantized rather than analog; RT operation needs sub-5-nm islands, and random background-charge offsets are the classic killer.

title: Gold-leaf electroscope: suspended graphene leaf holds charge in vacuum
idea: Store the bit as charge on a suspended graphene (or 20-nm SiN/Al) leaf in a sealed cavity, touching nothing but its clamp on thick thermal oxide; electrostatic repulsion deflects it a few nm, sensed capacitively by an underlying electrode without discharge, and charge is written or erased by field emission across a 5-nm vacuum gap to a sharp tip.
why: Facts 3 and 8: no junction or thin dielectric sits in the leakage path, so retention is set by negligible low-field emission, and read is non-destructive (no restore energy); built with graphene transfer, e-beam and critical-point drying; ns sensing of nm deflection is the risk.

title: Keyboard snap-dome: buckled nanomembrane holds bits mechanically
idea: Snap-dome keys and Venus flytraps use buckling bistability: deposit a 20-nm PECVD SiN membrane tuned to ~1 GPa compressive stress over a 300-nm cavity so it rests buckled up or down; electrostatic pulses from top or bottom electrodes snap it within ns (tiny mass, GHz modes), and its position sets a 3-5x capacitance difference read by the sense amp.
why: Zero-power non-volatile bit that cannot leak and ignores row hammer or radiation, with no contact wear because nothing touches; buildable with PECVD stress control, e-beam and HF release; ~300-nm membranes limit density.

title: Vinyl record pressing: nanoimprint-stamped storage-node arrays, no EUV
idea: Records are pressed from one nickel master: e-beam-write a single master of the storage-node hole array once, electroform nickel or Si daughter stamps, and replicate it on every wafer by UV nanoimprint followed by RIE and ALD fill; perfectly periodic cell arrays tolerate imprint defects far better than logic.
why: Fact 4 capital: replaces 1-3 EUV exposures (~$150M+ tool) for the storage-node layer with a ~$5M imprinter, cutting that layer's patterning capex 10-30x and easing a U.S. fab; a university e-beam writer plus imprinter can demonstrate 20-nm half-pitch arrays.

title: Swiss-roll pastry: strain-released self-rolling capacitor stack
idea: Deposit a planar TiN/Al2O3-HfO2/TiN stack on a strained SiNx bilayer over a sacrificial layer; selective release lets the built-in strain roll it into a 3-5-turn microtube, multiplying capacitor area per footprint ~10x from planar deposition only, like rolling a Swiss roll.
why: Facts 1 and 2: 3D capacitance with no high-AR etch, a natural fit for lateral capacitors in horizontal 3D DRAM; demonstrated with sputter, ALD and wet release in university labs; shrinking roll diameters below ~1 um is the risk.

title: Traffic-jam phases: charge-density-wave domain states in 1T-TaS2
idea: Traffic flips between free flow and jams; in 1T-TaS2 electrons lock into commensurate or nearly commensurate charge-density-wave states with ~10x resistance contrast, and thin flakes switch between metastable states under short current pulses; build two-terminal cells from exfoliated ~10-nm flakes with e-beam contacts and hBN encapsulation.
why: A collective electronic state holds the bit with no ions or defects moving, so endurance could be effectively unlimited with fJ-scale switching; the narrow room-temperature metastability window threatens retention at 85 C.

title: PERC solar back side: negative-charge Al2O3 fences carriers from storage node
idea: PERC solar cells use ALD Al2O3 carrying ~1e13 cm-2 negative fixed charge to repel minority carriers from surfaces; wrap storage-node junction sidewalls and isolation liners in 5-nm ALD Al2O3 so the field pushes the generation-active depletion edge away from defective interfaces, followed by forming-gas hydrogenation, demonstrated on university test diodes and gated capacitors.
why: Fact 3: perimeter interface generation dominates the leakage tail, so ~10x lower perimeter generation gives ~3-10x longer worst-cell retention using only ALD and a furnace.

title: Plywood veneer slicing: film-thickness-defined 5-nm electrode combs
idea: Veneer exposes the edges of thin layers: grow 40 alternating 5-nm ALD TiN/Al2O3 layers on a sidewall (or MBE GaAs/AlGaAs, then cleave) and use the exposed edge as a stamp or mask (SNAP-style) to transfer a 10-nm-pitch line array; cross two such arrays with ultrathin ZrO2 so each intersection is a storage capacitor for gain-cell or diode-isolated arrays.
why: Fact 4: 10-nm-pitch lines defined by film thickness rather than lithography, beyond EUV resolution with an ALD tool; fits a university fab; line fan-out contacts and crossbar sneak paths are the risks.

title: Thin-film battery plateau: two-phase lithium node holds voltage despite leakage
idea: A battery's flat voltage plateau barely moves as charge leaks, unlike a capacitor's linear droop; make each node a ~50-nm solid-state nanobattery (sputtered Li4Ti5O12 or LiFePO4 electrode, ~10-nm Li3PS4 or LiPON electrolyte) whose states are the charged and discharged plateaus, sensed by a gain transistor; ~1e5 stored Li+ outlast fA leakage.
why: Fact 3: at the 13 fA tail, 1e5 charges last ~1 s (~20x the refresh window) while the voltage stays digital, never drifting into the sense margin; buildable with sputter, evaporator and a glovebox; ionic write speed and cycle life are the risks.

title: Moire silk patterns: twist-angle-defined trap lattices as litho-free storage sites
idea: Moire fabric shows a large pattern from two fine weaves; twisting WSe2/WS2 bilayers by ~1-3 degrees creates a lattice of deep potential minima at ~8-10 nm pitch, each able to trap a hole; a 50-nm e-beam gate over a patch writes trapped-hole occupancy that shifts an underlying channel threshold, a floating-gate-like bit whose sites come from the twist, not lithography.
why: Density and litho: sub-10-nm storage sites with zero patterning, built with a twist-transfer stage, e-beam and hBN encapsulation; moire trap depths (~100-200 meV) give only ms-scale retention at room temperature unless deeper heterostructures are found.

title: Qubit-fab double-angle evaporation: self-aligned AlOx overlap storage capacitors
idea: Superconducting-qubit labs make Al/AlOx/Al junctions with one resist bridge and two angled evaporations plus in-situ oxidation; use this Dolan-bridge method to form the storage capacitor and its node contact in one e-beam exposure: first Al leg, controlled O2 dose for a 1.5-3-nm AlOx dielectric, then a second leg at a different angle whose overlap area, not the lithography, sets capacitance.
why: Capital and step count: capacitor plus contact in one exposure with zero overlay error, using an e-beam writer and angle evaporator; low-k AlOx limits charge, so it pairs with gain-cell or avalanche-sensed low-charge cells.

title: Optical rectenna MIM diodes: transistor-free diode-isolated storage node
idea: Optical rectennas rectify THz signals with metal-insulator-metal tunnel diodes whose work-function asymmetry gives strong rectification; isolate each storage capacitor with two back-to-back asymmetric MIIM diodes (e.g., Nb/Nb2O5/Al2O3/Pt), so the node charges only when row and column voltages exceed turn-on, enabling 4F2 crosspoint decks with no silicon transistor.
why: Facts 2 and 4: transistor-free 3D stacking where each deck is deposition plus relaxed litho, all with sputter, ALD and evaporation; diode off-current at hold must reach ~1e-18 A per cell, ~1e4 below published MIIM diodes.

title: Diatom biomineralization: DNA-origami templates place 10-nm storage nodes
idea: Diatoms grow silica shells on protein templates; adsorb DNA-origami tiles carrying metal seeds on a 10-nm grid onto shape-matched landing sites defined by relaxed e-beam litho, then grow storage nodes or floating islands from the seeds by ALD or electroless plating, burning off the origami afterward.
why: Fact 4: sub-12-nm feature placement without EUV using wet chemistry plus one relaxed-pitch e-beam step, all university-buildable; placement yield (~95-99% today versus >99.9999% needed) requires spare rows and ECC.

title: Coral and stalagmite growth: VLS nanowire forests grown as capacitor electrodes
idea: Grow the electrode instead of etching it: place Al, Sn or Cu catalyst dots (CMOS-friendlier than gold) by dewetting or e-beam litho, grow 1-2-um vertical Si or SnO2 nanowires by vapor-liquid-solid growth in a university LPCVD furnace, where 100:1 aspect ratios come for free, then ALD-coat the dielectric and top electrode.
why: Fact 1: AR >=100:1 electrodes with no 70:1 plasma etch or its EUV-defined mask, removing the hardest capacitor process; nanowire leaning, collapse and catalyst contamination are the risks.
